segments: The haters of Christians envied the Christian man who had been set in authority over them,
and they unsheathed swords and daggers,
and entered against him into the courtyard where he was residing,
and murdered him there,
on Monday [the 31st?]
in the month of Tammuz of that same year.
The sons of this man who was robbed of life quickly went to the camp,
and showed the insolence of the Arabs {Muslims} there.
And the order went forth
that the murderers should be executed,
and the citizens should be fined ten thousand (dinars of) gold.
And thus they arrived at the city,
and they killed seven or eight of the governors {satraps} there.
And at the beginning of the year one thousand six hundred and two [1602 of the Greeks = 1291 AD], slanders were brought against a certain Kurdish emir,
who was known as Shujāʿ al-Dīn {OCR?} the unjust,
from the region of the island of Qardū [Jazirat Ibn ʿUmar].
And his case was investigated before Baytmish the athlete {champion},
and he and one of his sons were put to death in the region of Mosul.
In those same days,
certain Ismaili men were sent in the guise of merchants to Mosul,
in order to spring upon the emirs and commanders in it and kill them,
so that no Christian or Jew might again have authority anywhere,
otherwise they would murder (them) secretly and subtly.
Therefore, when they arrived at Mosul,
and took lodging in one of the inns according to the custom of merchants,
they quarreled with one another,
and began to strive one with another.
A certain man who was near them and heard their dispute,
grasped {OCR?} the meaning of their conversation,
and went quickly and informed these emirs.
And they made haste, sent, and seized them.
And when they began to torture them,
an old man among them said:
"You do not need to torture us;
we three men came to kill you,
and three others went to Babylon {Baghdad}
to kill the Jew who is there,
and three others went to the camp
to kill the Sahib-Diwan there."
Then at that very hour they impaled these men,
and they sent to Babylon {Baghdad}, seized those others also easily, and put them to death.
As for those, however, who went to the camp,
their request was speedily granted,
and their objective was fulfilled without toil or fatigue.
